The Legal Counsel plays a critical role in protecting the Group's legal and commercial interests while ensuring compliance with applicable Saudi laws and regulations. This role provides practical legal guidance to management and business functions, manages litigation and debt recovery proceedings, and oversees legal matters across commercial, corporate, and employment-related areas. Working closely with the Collections, Finance, HR, and business teams, you will help mitigate legal risks, safeguard company assets and receivables, and support sound business decisions across the organization.
q: Bachelor's degree in law, with a valid legal license and eligibility to practice and represent companies before judicial authorities in Saudi Arabia.
Proven practical experience in commercial litigation, debt recovery, enforcement procedures, and corporate legal advisory within the Saudi market.
Strong working knowledge of Saudi legal frameworks, particularly the Companies Law, Civil Transactions Law, and Labor Law.
Hands-on experience with the Najiz platform, Enforcement Courts, promissory notes, executable instruments, and court proceedings.
Demonstrated experience drafting, reviewing, and negotiating commercial contracts, settlement agreements, legal notices, and litigation documents.
Experience handling employment-related legal matters, including labor disputes, investigations, disciplinary actions, and terminations.
Strong understanding of corporate governance, regulatory compliance, commercial licensing, and corporate documentation.
Excellent negotiation, analytical, communication, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to translate complex legal matters into practical business recommendations.
High level of integrity, sound judgement, attention to detail, and ability to manage multiple legal cases and priorities independently.
r: Partner with senior management and internal departments to provide practical legal advice on commercial, corporate, regulatory, and employment-related matters under Saudi Arabian law.

Work closely with the Collections Department to review overdue customer accounts, assess legal documentation and evaluate recovery options, including contracts, invoices, promissory notes, and cheques.
Prepare and issue formal legal notices and demand letters, and draft settlement agreements and payment rescheduling arrangements to protect the Group's interests.

Manage legal proceedings, including preparing statements of claim, defense memoranda, appeals, and other legal submissions, while representing the company before Commercial, General, and Labor Courts and relevant quasi-judicial authorities.
File, monitor, and follow up on lawsuits and attend court hearings, both in person and remotely, ensuring timely handling and resolution of legal cases.

Manage enforcement proceedings through the Najiz platform and Enforcement Courts, including applications involving executable instruments, court judgments, asset attachments, and travel ban orders, following through until recovery is achieved.

Draft, review, and negotiate commercial agreements, including client and vendor contracts, credit facility agreements, non-disclosure agreements (NDAs), and other business-related arrangements, ensuring appropriate legal protections and risk mitigation.
Ensure contractual terms and conditions adequately safeguard the Group against financial exposure, payment defaults, and commercial disputes.
Monitor changes in Saudi laws and regulations, including the Companies Law, Civil Transactions Law, and Labor Law, and advise on their implications for the business.

Support HR on employment-related legal matters, including employment contracts, work organization bylaws, internal investigations, disciplinary actions, and employee terminations in line with Saudi Labor Law.
Represent the company in employment-related disputes before amicable settlement offices and Labor Courts, whenever required.

Oversee corporate legal documentation and records, including Commercial Registrations (CRs), partners' resolutions, powers of attorney (POAs), licensing matters, and intellectual property and trademark protection.
Work collaboratively with Finance, Collections, HR, and business stakeholders to identify legal risks, strengthen internal controls, and promote compliance across the organization.

d: The Warehouse Specialist supports Installation Support Services (ISS) operations at Al Udeid Air Base (AUAB), Qatar. The position is responsible for receiving, storing, inventorying, issuing, tracking, safeguarding, and transporting Government Furnished Material, repair parts, bench stock, consumable supplies, lodging maintenance items, recreational program supplies, and other contract-related property. The Warehouse Specialist ensures compliance with AFCAP V, FAR Part 45, property accountability requirements, inventory controls, safety standards, and all applicable PWS requirements.
q: Shall be a USN and have at least 3 years of warehouse, logistics, supply, property management, or inventory control experience or comparable civilian experience.
High school diploma required; associate degree in logistics, supply chain management, business, or related field preferred.
Experience receiving, storing, issuing, and tracking inventory using automated systems and Microsoft Office applications.
Knowledge of Government Property accountability principles, inventory management, stock control, and warehouse operations.
Ability to operate forklifts and material handling equipment; forklift certification required.
Possess a valid US driver's license and US passport.
Ability to adapt to frequent change and a hectic, fast-paced work environment.
Outstanding problem-solving skills and sound judgment.
Ability to read, write, and communicate effectively in English.
Must be able to obtain and maintain facility credentials/authorization. Note: US Citizenship is required for facility credentials/authorization at this work location.
Ability to lift 50 pounds and work in warehouse and outdoor environments.
Experience supporting deployed or austere operations preferred.
Experience with working and communicating with the Government or military personnel.
Work Environment, Physical Demands, and Mental Demands
Availability to work extended hours, 6-day workweeks, and support 24/7 operations as mission requires.
Able to lift, carry, and push supplies and boxes up to 50 pounds.
The physical demands described here are representative of those that an employee may perform on an occasional to regular basis while performing functions of this job.
Exposure to desert climate, prolonged standing, and facility walkthroughs.
Must operate in a deployed, austere environment with high operational tempo.
Must have the ability to work well with others, to include the Government.
Frequent standing, walking, bending, lifting, pushing, pulling, and material handling activities.
Exposure to warehouse operations, outdoor environments, desert climate conditions, and loading/unloading activities.
Must work effectively with Government personnel, subcontractors, and multinational workforces.
r: Receive, inspect, inventory, store, issue, and account for Government Furnished Material (GFM), consumables, repair parts, bench stock, equipment, furnishings, linens, appliances, and maintenance supplies.
Maintain accurate warehouse inventories with no discrepancies and support Government Property accountability requirements.
Accept vendor deliveries at installation entry points and coordinate transportation, unloading, storage, and distribution of materials.
Operate warehouse equipment including forklifts and material handling equipment in accordance with safety requirements.
Maintain detailed stock records, reorder points, receiving documentation, issue logs, property tracking, and inventory reports.
Support lodging maintenance, recreational services, custodial services, linen services, and HAMS operations through timely issue of materials and equipment.
Identify supply shortages and prepare requisitions, AF Form 9 documentation, quotations, and supporting procurement paperwork per PWS 4.11.
Establish and maintain bench stock levels and inventory controls for frequently used repair parts and consumables.
Conduct inventories, cycle counts, reconciliation, and property inspections; report loss, theft, damage, or destruction immediately.
Coordinate transportation of supplies, equipment, and repair parts across AUAB service locations.
Assist with transition inventories, property turnover, equipment accountability, and contract closeout activities.
Maintain warehouse organization, cleanliness, safety, labeling, storage segregation, and hazardous material compliance.
Support monthly reports, inventory reports, fuel reports, property reports, and other contractual deliverables.
Monitor serviceability of warehouse equipment and coordinate repairs when required.
Provide escort and accountability support for LN/OCN personnel when assigned and authorized.

Must comply with Government Property management requirements, FAR Part 45, AFCAP property accountability procedures, warehouse inventory controls, bench stock management, receiving and distribution requirements, work-order support processes, reporting requirements, hazardous material controls, and safety requirements contained in Sections 3.1, 4.6, 4.10, 4.11, 9.0, 10.0, Appendix G, and Appendix H of the ISS PWS.
Perform other duties assigned by Site Management.
